sources.name: Global mercury monitoring in biota
sources.publisher: United Nations Environment Programme Global Mercury Partnership

assessment.node_boundary: The generic heavy-metal node is quantified with two explicit sentinel metals: mercury for environmental persistence, global transport and food-web bioaccumulation; lead for the measured global human-health burden. The receipt is not a complete inventory of all heavy metals.

global_extent.basis: UNEP identifies mercury as a global concern because of long-range atmospheric transport, persistence and bioaccumulation; WHO describes widespread lead contamination and exposure globally.

uncertainty: The environmental and health indicators describe different sentinel metals and assessment years. They establish a quantitative global accumulated burden for the broad heavy-metal node but must not be interpreted as a combined-metal incidence estimate or as causal attribution of the WHO lead burden to mercury.
